Review-003’s sole Spec Must is dismissed as an attempt to reopen the settled caller/package boundary; no repair is authorized.

The admitted design-recheck receipt expressly dismissed O1: package validation owns intrinsic Fixer receipt shape/state only, while the caller retains the typed Judge receipt and dispatch context and therefore mechanically enforces contextual presence/absence and exact order-insensitive set equality without parsing the opaque fix packet. Current HEAD implements that ruling: `classesRepaired` is optional in the Fixer schema/type, is accepted only for completed Fixer receipts, and—when present—has the required intrinsic shape and unique comma-free names (`src/worker-role.ts`, `src/package-contracts/worker-output.ts`). `README.md` accurately assigns contextual reconciliation to the caller.

No later owner evidence changed O1. The owner-resolution comment adopted option 1 solely to close O2’s key-grammar gate and states that all other Issue #31 decisions remain unchanged; the subsequent owner-resolution judgment likewise says O1 was already dismissed and must not be reopened. The original combination law remains a caller-enforced contextual requirement, not a package-local requirement that every completed Fixer receipt include `classesRepaired`.

The two previously repaired classes reported clean by Review-003 are not reopened. Fixer audit/closure automation remains out of scope under #12.
